stories.title: Employment Tribunal claims surge beyond resolutions
stories.ltme_summary: Solicitors Journal reports, citing Ministry of Justice data, that Employment Tribunal claims reached 25,000 in the first quarter of 2026/27 against 10,000 disposals, giving an open caseload of 537,000. Fieldfisher's report links delays to reforms due in 2027 and to AI, with Alex Watson quoted on delay.
stories.hook: Employment Tribunal open caseload reaches 537,000 as claims outpace disposals

stories.title: Dentons showcases commitment to responsible business
New directory simplifies finding expert witnesses
Birketts advises on Azpects sale
stories.ltme_summary: Solicitors Journal reports that Birketts LLP advised the majority sellers of Azpects Group on its sale to Sika. The sale covers UK entities Unitech Innovations, Azpects and Building Chemical Research (1984), with US operations sold with help from US counsel. Emma Bysouth led the Birketts team.
stories.hook: Birketts advises majority sellers on Azpects sale to Sika

stories.title: Fake AI Citations Are Falling. Subtler Errors May Be Taking Their Place
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Tech Monitor reports that court filings containing AI hallucinations have fallen for two consecutive quarters. Researchers and judges warn that subtler errors, such as real cases cited for propositions they do not support, may be harder to detect.
stories.hook: AI citation hallucinations fall in court filings, but subtler errors may be rising

Harvard Law School suspends students’ access to library after ‘study-in’
TX Prosecutor Moons Senators In Desperate Bid For Attention
62 Organizations Call On Congress To Advance 4 Medicare Reforms
AI Slop Or Novel Arguments? A Texas Judge Goes Off The Rails
stories.ltme_summary: Above the Law comments on a Texas federal case, reported by Business Insider, in which Judge Mark Pittman criticised three lawyers' motions as AI slop and threatened sanctions. The lawyers say they used AI, disclosed it under local rules and wrote the arguments themselves. The column questions whether judges should disparage lawyers for suspected AI-written work.
stories.hook: Texas judge calls motions AI slop and threatens sanctions, lawyers deny AI wrote them

stories.title: HSF Kramer Hires 6 Legal Engineers from Norm.AI
stories.ltme_summary: Artificial Lawyer reports that HSF Kramer has hired six legal engineers from Norm.AI to join its global AI team, led by Chief AI Officer Ilona Logvinova. Justin D'Agostino, the firm's global CEO, says the hires show the firm is embedding AI across its practices. The article notes the move is talent leaving an AI-native firm for a large firm.
stories.hook: HSF Kramer hires six legal engineers from AI-native Norm.AI

stories.title: Baker McKenzie Shows the Way with Billable Hour Shift
stories.hook: Baker McKenzie global chair says billable hour will no longer be the default

stories.title: HSF Kramer Recruits Specialist Engineers For AI Push
Aderant Says It Milana Docketing Product, Launched In 2022, Is Now In Nearly 40% of Am Law 200 Firms
stories.hook: Aderant says its Milana docketing product is now in nearly 40% of Am Law 200 firms

stories.title: On LawNext: Live from ClioCon, Jack Newton on Clio’s ‘Refounding,’ Its Push into the Courts, and Why Data Is the Only Durable Moat
stories.ltme_summary: In a LawNext podcast recorded at ClioCon 2026 in Boston, Clio founder and CEO Jack Newton discusses what he calls a refounding of the company, its agentic AI launches and its push into the courts. He says Clio has hired Pablo Arredondo and Bridget McCormack and acquired Learned Hand. Newton argues that data, including vLex's documents and Clio Docket filings, is the company's main moat.
stories.hook: Clio's Jack Newton says data is the company's moat as it moves into the courts

stories.title: Paul Hastings set to hire seven-partner, 20-lawyer Weil team for German buildout
stories.hook: Paul Hastings set to take seven Weil partners in Germany as Weil winds down

stories.title: Simpson Thacher takes on Weil trainees as ‘profoundly difficult and emotional’ wind-down begins
King & Spalding’s Gary Born on falling into law, switching firms and going to extremes for witness statements
Clients ten times more likely to follow their partner after a move, new data shows
Simpson Thacher brings London TC launch forward to rescue stranded Weil future trainees
Bye bye, billable hour? Bakers rethinks how it charges clients
Barrister suspended after pursuing case that was ‘waste of his client’s money’
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Cheek reports that the Bar Standards Board tribunal suspended barrister Emil Mihai Lixandru for 12 months after he pursued a judicial review that was an abuse of process. Seven misconduct charges were found proven. The findings remain subject to appeal.
stories.hook: Barrister Emil Lixandru suspended for 12 months over abusive judicial review

stories.title: Monday morning round-up
The legal architecture behind scalable partnerships
stories.ltme_summary: A sponsored Legal Futures piece by LexisNexis argues that partnerships need legal input on customer ownership, data control, liability and IP before they can scale. It refers to the Incredible innovations report and cites Rolls-Royce's TotalCare model as an example of contracts shaping value.
stories.hook: LexisNexis says partnerships stall unless legal settles data and liability first

stories.title: Legal AI is moving deeper into legal workflows – is your firm ready?
stories.ltme_summary: A sponsored Legal Futures piece by OneAdvanced argues that firms must check whether their data, permissions and workflows are ready before adopting agentic AI. It says AI readiness is increasingly an information architecture challenge and links AI governance to information governance, citing Legal IT Insider research on security and risk.
stories.hook: OneAdvanced argues law firms must fix data and permissions before agentic AI

stories.title: HSF Kramer hires team of legal engineers from Norm AI
stories.ltme_summary: HSF Kramer has hired a team of legal engineers from Norm AI, according to Legal IT Insider. The extract available to us is only a site verification notice, so the number of hires and the role details cannot be confirmed from it.
stories.hook: HSF Kramer hires a team of legal engineers from Norm AI

stories.title: Weil’s AI-native Big Law challenger in talks to raise ‘hundreds of millions’ before firm’s collapse, report says
Crosby takes lawyers out of the loop after securing $5m cover for AI agents
stories.ltme_summary: Nonbillable reports that New York AI law firm Crosby has secured a $5m insurance policy from Testudo covering its AI agents, effective 3 November. Crosby says it has removed lawyer oversight from tasks around 20 per cent of its work, which it calls paralegal tasks. It expects 15 agents per lawyer by the end of 2026.
stories.hook: Crosby removes lawyer oversight from 20% of work after $5m AI agent cover

stories.title: Simpson Thacher brings forward London training contract launch to take Weil recruits
Big Law’s billable hour faces a fresh challenge as Baker McKenzie changes course
Consumer champion calls for COLP separation principle to stand
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society Gazette reports that the Legal Services Consumer Panel has urged the SRA not to abandon its plan to separate compliance officer and management roles at firms. The SRA has paused the rule, which would have applied to firms above £600,000 turnover or holding over £2m client money, after opposition from smaller firms.
stories.hook: Consumer panel urges SRA not to drop COLP and COFA separation after rule pause

stories.title: Automatic pardons for abortion offences relating to women's own pregnancies
stories.ltme_summary: The Ministry of Justice has announced that women in England and Wales convicted, cautioned, arrested or investigated for abortion offences relating to their own pregnancy will be automatically pardoned, with records deleted. Section 242 of the Crime and Policing Act 2026 provides the basis, and the change takes effect from 16 November 2026.
stories.hook: Women in England and Wales get automatic pardons for own-pregnancy abortion offences

stories.title: Lawyers told to release skeleton arguments and witness statements
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society Gazette reports that Mr Justice Nicklin, who chairs the judiciary's transparency and openness board, urged lawyers to make skeleton arguments and witness statements available to reporters. He described failure to do so as tantamount to secret justice. The article outlines Court of Appeal and commercial court document pilots.
stories.hook: Mr Justice Nicklin tells lawyers to open skeleton arguments and witness statements to reporters

stories.title: Lady chief justice urges caution over rape trial reform
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society Gazette reports that the lady chief justice, Baroness Carr, said debate on rape trial conduct is not fully informed and urged caution over legislating jury directions. Speaking at the Bar Council conference, she said judges already give rape myth directions. The Ministry of Justice says it will consider any proposal.
stories.hook: Lady chief justice warns against legislating jury directions in rape trials

stories.title: UK Abortion Pardons Take Effect as Law Requires Criminal Record Deletion
Johnson Controls Agrees $5m Cybersecurity Settlement Under False Claims Act
Taking care of an unoccupied property if you live abroad

stories.hook: Ministry of Justice seeks evidence on section 9(3) of the Human Rights Act by January 2027

stories.title: ABA Legal Ed council votes to loosen faculty, course requirements in accreditation standards
Judge releases DUI suspect after reading AI-assisted police report disclosure
stories.ltme_summary: The ABA Journal reports that an Arizona judge released a DUI suspect, Anthony Edward Rene Quidera, after finding no probable cause once the court learned the arresting officer had used an AI tool, Truleo AI, to draft the arrest report. The report carried a disclosure of AI assistance. Maricopa County Superior Court commissioner Daniel Fenzel said he could not weigh whether generative AI wrote parts of the narrative. The arrest was on 29 October.
stories.hook: Arizona commissioner frees DUI suspect after police report disclosed Truleo AI drafting, citing inability to test probable cause

Access To Justice Hackathon Kicks Off
Did Cahill Gordon’s ‘Rescuer’ Get Revealed?
The 2027 Law Firm Pulse Report: An In-House View
stories.ltme_summary: Above the Law, with research from InsightDynamo and Listen Labs, presents a Pulse Report on in-house sentiment ahead of Q4 law firm rate rises. InsightDynamo surveyed 750 legal budget decision-makers at companies with revenue of at least $1 billion this autumn, and Listen Labs ran 25 interviews. The report covers outside counsel rates for 2024 to 2026, expected rate increases, insourcing and legal technology disruption.
stories.hook: Survey of 750 in-house budget decision-makers finds law departments weighing firm rate rises against AI-driven insourcing

Lexpert Rising Stars Awards 2026

Biz Development Tip Of The Month: Focus On Client Service
What's Holding Back More Judges From Using AI
Exclusive: MinuteBox Launches AI Agent to Turn Its Entity Management Database Into a ‘System of Work’
stories.ltme_summary: MinuteBox has launched an AI agent that lets legal teams query corporate entity records, order registry reports, draft documents from firm precedents and record changes. CEO Daniel Levine told LawSites the product is the first of three AI releases planned. The agent is an optional per-seat feature, designed for paralegals and lawyers.
stories.hook: MinuteBox launches an AI agent that turns its entity records into a platform for legal work

stories.title: LEAP Legal Software
stories.ltme_summary: LEAP, a UK cloud practice management vendor, presents its platform as an all-in-one system covering case management, accounting, document management, publishing and AI. The company says it reinvests over £13 million a year in research and development. The piece is promotional copy in LEAP's own words, and it sits alongside an interview with CEO Craig Matthews about AI efficiency at LegalEx London.
stories.hook: LEAP says it reinvests over £13m a year in R&D as it pitches an all-in-one cloud platform with AI to UK law firms

stories.title: Clio: Expanded functionality and a changing competitive landscape
stories.ltme_summary: Legal IT Insider has published a piece titled on Clio, which covers expanded functionality and a changing competitive landscape. The extract available is only a site verification message, so the product changes and competitors discussed cannot be confirmed from this text. Clio is a practice management provider used by law firms.
stories.hook: Clio's expanded functionality is set against a shifting competitive landscape for practice management

stories.title: Ashurst Perkins Coie, Macfarlanes act on £1.2bn UK wealth manager sale
Consumer panel calls for COLP separation principle to stand
stories.ltme_summary: The Legal Services Consumer Panel urges the SRA not to drop plans to separate compliance officer and management roles in firms. Writing in a blog, panel member Adhir Ramdarshan says the pause should improve the safeguard rather than abandon it. The SRA has paused the rule, which would have applied to firms with turnover above £600,000 or more than £2m in client money.
stories.hook: Consumer panel urges SRA to keep COLP and COFA separation after pausing the rule

Vancouver firm Jiwaji Law hires lawyers with backgrounds in securities law, influencer relations
stories.ltme_summary: Vancouver boutique Jiwaji Law has added two lawyers, Priya Parihar from DWF Group and Olivia Armstrong from Kornfeld LLP, bringing headcount to six. Co-founder Aneka Jiwaji says growth is driven by client demand. The firm was launched last year by sisters Aneka and Afshaan Jiwaji as a women-led, women-owned business.
stories.hook: Jiwaji Law hires two lawyers in Vancouver, taking headcount to six

AI-driven conveyancing start-up set to expand nationally
stories.ltme_summary: Koala Legal, an AI-driven conveyancing start-up, plans to expand nationally after opening in Sheffield, according to co-founder Ashley Tate speaking to Legal Futures. The firm received its Council for Licensed Conveyancers licence in April and says it is on most lenders' panels. Its work mainly comes from Sheffield estate agents, and Tate says the firm is not marketing itself as AI first.
stories.hook: Koala Legal plans a national rollout after its Sheffield launch, working mainly through estate agents

stories.title: Campaign for ‘no win, no fee’ ban points finger at funding too
stories.ltme_summary: The Fair Civil Justice campaign launched a film in Parliament calling for a ban on 'no win, no fee' wording in consumer advertising and for statutory regulation of litigation funding. The film follows Burnley homeowners pursued for costs by collapsed SSB Law. The campaign cites SRA research showing 21 per cent of consumers were told possible costs before signing up.
stories.hook: Fair Civil Justice seeks a ban on 'no win, no fee' advertising after the SSB Law collapse

stories.title: Bar Standards Board sets diversity targets for its managers
stories.ltme_summary: The Bar Standards Board has set a target for 25 to 30 per cent of its managers to come from ethnic minority backgrounds by 2031, after the share fell to 17 per cent in 2025-26.

stories.title: “Organisational” divorce app aims to help LiPs and law firm clients
stories.ltme_summary: Divorcify, a UK app launched by digital marketing manager Martin Cleverley, helps people organise divorce documents and prepare questions for advisers. Cleverley says it uses a form of ChatGPT, costs up to £4.99 a month and is aimed at litigants in person as well as clients of solicitors and barristers. He says he funded it himself and is not seeking outside investment. Divorcify is marketed through a partnership with AndysManClub.
stories.hook: Divorcify launches an AI-based app for divorce document organisation, aimed at litigants in person and solicitors' clients

stories.title: The AI competence test every junior solicitor should pass
stories.ltme_summary: Dr Gleb Tsipursky argues that law firms should test junior solicitors' ability to explain AI-assisted work, not just produce it. He refers to the SRA consultation, open from 8 October to 3 December 2026, on updating the Statement of Solicitor Competence to cover technology and AI, with final versions expected in April 2027. He also cites a Pinsent Masons case involving misleading AI-drafted letters to the High Court.
stories.hook: Tsipursky urges law firms to test whether juniors can explain AI-assisted work before the SRA competence changes

stories.ltme_summary: Perplexity has replaced its counsel in Reddit v. SerpApi, switching from Keker Van Nest and a proposed Proskauer team to Mayer Brown attorneys Allison Aviki and Elisabeth Anderson, according to the commentary.

stories.title: Emerging AI guidance for financial institutions – A visual comparison of the OCC and FSB AI frameworks
stories.ltme_summary: Davis Polk compares the OCC's new supervisory framework for banks' AI use with the FSB's finalised sound practices for responsible AI adoption. The firm's visual guide sets out where the two frameworks align and diverge.

stories.title: Kirkland Advises Peak Rock Capital-Backed Seagull Software on Sale to Loftware | News | Kirkland & Ellis LLP
stories.ltme_summary: Kirkland & Ellis says it advised Peak Rock Capital on the sale of its portfolio company Seagull Software, maker of BarTender, to Loftware. The deal combines two labelling and product identification businesses. The Kirkland team included corporate lawyers Brendan Caldon, Matthew Goulding, Alec Manzer, Dan O'Connor and EJ Chang, with tax lawyer Roger Lucas.
stories.hook: Kirkland advises Peak Rock Capital on the sale of Seagull Software to Loftware

stories.title: AI-Generated Content Compliance Under Article 50 of the EU AI Act
stories.ltme_summary: Shakespeare Martineau sets out what Article 50 of the EU AI Act requires of UK organisations, with transparency duties applying from 2 August 2026. It lists four obligations for providers and deployers and penalties of up to 3 per cent of worldwide turnover or EUR 15m. It also points to the Commission's voluntary Code of Practice of 10 June 2026 and its guidelines of 20 July 2026.
stories.hook: Shakespeare Martineau says UK firms selling into the EU must meet Article 50 AI transparency duties

stories.title: Harrison Drury expands with new office
Tonkean Alternatives for Legal Teams: 2026 Comparison
stories.ltme_summary: Neota Logic publishes a 2026 comparison positioning its governed AI workflow platform as an alternative to Tonkean for legal teams. The piece argues legal needs deterministic rules, logging and human checkpoints. It cites a Hyperion Research guide from October 2024 that lists Tonkean among legal workflow tools. The article is vendor marketing for Neota Logic.
stories.hook: Neota Logic pitches its governed workflows as the better choice than Tonkean for legal teams

stories.title: Contract Management Security | Summize
stories.ltme_summary: Summize, a contract management vendor, publishes guidance on securing contract data across access, data protection and process control. It cites WorldCC and Deloitte research that organisations hold contracts across 24 systems on average, and IBM's 2025 figure of $4.92m for breaches involving malicious insiders. The page is marketing content.
stories.hook: Summize says contracts spread across 24 systems on average create a security blind spot

stories.title: One Year in San Diego: Building Our West Coast Team | Summize
stories.ltme_summary: Summize marks almost a year since opening its San Diego office in November 2025. The company says the team now covers sales development, account executives, pre-sales and implementation, following earlier offices in Boston and Manchester.

stories.title: UC Law San Francisco Launches AI Tool Building Course for Lawyers
stories.ltme_summary: UC Law San Francisco has launched a three-day course, the Law and AI Certificate Lab, on building AI legal tools and the ethical issues involved, according to Legal Tech Monitor. The extract is brief and does not give the course fee, start dates or intake size.
stories.hook: UC Law San Francisco offers a three-day lab on building AI legal tools for lawyers

stories.title: Richards, Layton & Finger Attorney Sanctioned $2,500 for Brief With AI Hallucinations
stories.ltme_summary: Vice Chancellor Lori Will of the Delaware Court of Chancery sanctioned a Richards, Layton & Finger attorney $2,500 over a brief containing AI-generated hallucinations, according to Legal Tech Monitor. The court declined to sanction the firm itself, citing its efforts to prevent misuse of generative AI.
stories.hook: Delaware Chancery sanctions a Richards, Layton & Finger attorney $2,500 over AI hallucinations

stories.title: Rising AI Adoption Hasn't Yet Broadly Impacted the Billable Hour, Legal Hiring
stories.ltme_summary: A Relativity report finds that AI adoption is now near-ubiquitous in legal work, but predicted widespread job losses and a shift away from the billable hour have not happened, according to Legal Tech Monitor. The extract does not give the survey sample or methodology.
stories.hook: Relativity report finds AI has not yet reshaped the billable hour or legal hiring

stories.title: Are Legal Departments Rushing Into AI Without Getting Their House in Order?
stories.ltme_summary: Keao Caindec argues that AI tools perform better when they draw on information across a company's legal operations rather than separate systems. Legal Tech Monitor reports internal tests at Clarra, a California company, which found that consolidating data improved AI performance sixfold and token efficiency by about 80 per cent.
stories.hook: Clarra says consolidating legal operations data lifted AI performance sixfold in internal tests

stories.title: Digital Twin Startup Twin1 Adds $5M to Seed Round
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Tech Monitor reports that Twin1, a digital twin start-up backed by Orrick, has added $5m to its seed round. The company plans to use the money to hire and expand deployments at law firms and other customers. The extract is brief and does not name the investors in the new round.
stories.hook: Twin1 adds $5m to its seed round to expand law firm deployments

stories.title: How to Redact Documents and Metadata Thoroughly: eDiscovery Webinars
stories.ltme_summary: Doug Austin of eDiscovery Today promotes a free Lexbe webinar on 18 November 2026 about redacting documents and metadata in Lexbe. The session covers redaction layers, email header fields and a production checklist. Lexbe is a sponsor of the blog, which the post discloses.
stories.hook: Lexbe webinar on 18 November shows how to redact text and metadata before production

stories.title: Everlaw Surpasses $200 Million Run Rate
stories.ltme_summary: Everlaw, the AI-powered litigation platform, says it has passed a $200m annualised revenue run rate and serves more than 1,700 customers. The company says its run rate doubled in three years and that monthly requests through connected AI assistants grew more than 7,600 per cent from June to October 2026. Doug Austin repeats the release with congratulations.
stories.hook: Everlaw says its annualised revenue run rate has passed $200m as AI assistants connect to its platform

stories.title: Cahill’s Mystery Suitor Is DLA Piper. Or Willkie. What The Domain Registrations Tell Us — See Also
stories.ltme_summary: Above the Law reports on domain registrations suggesting DLA Piper or Willkie may be the firm approaching Cahill, alongside brief items on Biglaw recruiting and salary scales.

5 Reasons Insurers Blame Riverhead Motorcycle Riders
HSF Kramer’s Australian Profits Stall While the Global Firm Celebrates
Wotton Kearney Adopts Harvey Firmwide Across Asia Pacific
stories.ltme_summary: Wotton Kearney, an insurance and risk law firm in Asia Pacific, is rolling out Harvey firmwide across its 14 offices in Australia, New Zealand, Singapore and Thailand. The firm says a six-month pilot with 200 users reached a 94 per cent adoption rate and more than 30,000 queries. Its chief technology and AI officer and Harvey's APAC strategy director are quoted.
stories.hook: Wotton Kearney rolls out Harvey firmwide across Asia Pacific after a 94 per cent pilot adoption rate

stories.title: What Questions Come Up After Drugs Are Found in a Car?
AI firms says it is ‘replacing the traditional law firm’ after securing £15m funding
stories.ltme_summary: An AI firm says it is replacing the traditional law firm after raising £15m in funding, according to Today's Conveyancer. The article is a short opening extract, so the company's name, the investors and the scope of its services are not yet clear from what is available here. The piece sits in a conveyancing and property trade title.
stories.hook: An AI firm claims it is replacing the traditional law firm after a £15m funding round

[APAC] Expert Sierra Migration: Ask the Cloud Experts
stories.ltme_summary: Aderant has published a recording of a webinar, held on 12 November 2026, on migrating firms from Expert On-Prem to Expert Sierra. Speakers George Hernandez and Ryan Moffitt address timing, data and workflow questions. The recording lasts 51 minutes and is aimed at APAC audiences.
stories.hook: Aderant recording covers moving firms from Expert On-Prem to Expert Sierra in the cloud

stories.title: [APAC] Expert Sierra Migration: Ask the Cloud Experts
stories.ltme_summary: Aderant has republished its webinar recording on migrating firms to Expert Sierra, held on 12 November 2026 and lasting 51 minutes. Speakers George Hernandez and Ryan Moffitt take questions on timing, data and workflows. This is a duplicate of the APAC listing with the same content.
stories.hook: Aderant republishes its Expert Sierra migration webinar, a duplicate of the APAC listing

stories.title: More than 170 Law Firms, Including 40% of the Am Law 200, Trust Aderant Milana for Cloud Docketing
stories.ltme_summary: Aderant says its cloud docketing product Milana has been adopted by nearly 40 per cent of Am Law 200 firms and deployed at more than 170 firms since its 2022 launch. The release cites Troutman Pepper Locke and Yetter Coleman as users, and describes AI features including document intelligence and custom rules. The figures come from the vendor's own announcement dated 16 November 2026.
stories.hook: Aderant says Milana docketing has reached nearly 40 per cent of Am Law 200 firms

stories.title: Why a Lower Hourly Rate Doesn’t Always Mean Lower Legal Spend
stories.ltme_summary: Onit argues that lower hourly rates do not reliably cut outside counsel spend, citing staffing mix and billing guideline compliance. Onit executives Jeffrey Solomon and Matt DenOuden are quoted on the point.

stories.title: Is your law firm ready for the next decade?
stories.ltme_summary: Osprey Approach, with Legal News Wales, publishes a Welsh Legal Sector Transformation Report 2026 based on responses from more than 50 firms and in-house teams. It finds 48 per cent of respondents doubt or are unsure their current business model will last ten years. Firms without a recent valuation were more likely to consider a merger, the report says.
stories.hook: Osprey Approach finds 48 per cent of Welsh law firms unsure their business model will last ten years
